content.title: Complete a guest bouquet order on a phone
content.intent: Prove that a visitor can add an in-stock bouquet, see the basket total update, complete checkout without creating an account, and reach an order confirmation with an order number on a phone-sized web surface.
content.technique_notes: Techniques applied: equivalence partitioning for the successful in-stock/guest/non-Sunday order path; state / flow because the source describes an end-to-end checkout journey; persistence/responsiveness were not separately minted because the source promises phone completion, not refresh or multi-breakpoint behavior. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was needed because this scenario fixes one successful combination and the outcome-changing variants became separate scenarios under the outcome rule.

content.title: Block Sunday delivery selection during guest checkout
content.intent: Prove that Sunday cannot be chosen as the delivery date during bouquet checkout.
content.technique_notes: Techniques applied: negative / error and equivalence partitioning on delivery-date eligibility, separating the forbidden Sunday class from selectable non-Sunday dates. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was needed because the source names a single forbidden value class that changes the outcome.

content.title: Prevent adding an out-of-stock bouquet to the basket
content.intent: Prove that an out-of-stock bouquet cannot be added to the basket.
content.technique_notes: Techniques applied: negative / error and equivalence partitioning on stock state, separating addable in-stock bouquets from forbidden out-of-stock bouquets. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering array was needed because stock state is the single outcome-changing input for this rule.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Ranked highest because it is the end-to-end revenue path on the required phone surface and covers the most business-critical promises in one journey.
[value_score] Ranked second because Sunday blocking is an explicit fulfillment rule; allowing it would permit orders the florist cannot deliver.
[value_score] Ranked third because stock gating prevents failed or misleading purchase attempts, but it affects a narrower part of the flow than the happy path and delivery-date rule.
